<@U02GQL9QG9G> to bring you up to speed:

Once the aurora migration is completed this evening, we will have to submit another version of the app for approval since it is technically a new build. In an ideal world, the first version of the app would be the aurora migrated one so the team doesn't have to worry about supporting two backend versions with users on them. Alternatively, we think the best option is to go ahead and release the build that was already approved today since it will be unlisted. We'll submit the aurora-migrated version next week, which should be approved before any creator posts go out given we aren't changing any features, and before we see an uptick in new users.

Let us know if you're ok with this plan, and <@U05BV05GYQH> will push the button :slightly_smiling_face:

Also re: unlisted. A little more on my research for moving from unlisted --> public. I had to make a case for why we should be unlisted to Apple in the submission process. You can see what I wrote <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Eq3Np0jfWi5Y9SoHYCC0rAM51mnHdXEbbwk1DnF1BrM/edit?tab=t.0|here>.

To reduce the chances of rejection, it's recommended that we don't submit a request to switch to public for ~4 weeks to show that we have had time to assess our strategy laid out in the unlisted request. I think this is fine as it lines up well with our plans for when we will remove the waitlist

```export interface PostUploadManifest {
  version: '1.0'

  userId: string
  post: {
    caption: string
    topicIds?: string[]
    sources?: string[]
    isPremium?: boolean
    isCommentingEnabled?: boolean

    /** Additional metadata (stored as JSONB) */
    metadata?: Record<string, unknown>
  }

  /** Media items*/
  items: Array<{
    fileName: string
    mediaType: MediaType
    /** Sort order for carousel ordering (0, 1, 2...)*/
    sortOrder: number
    metadata?: {
      width?: number
      height?: number
      duration?: number
      fileSize?: number
      mimeType?: string
    }
  }>
}```

To clarify - there are a few things happening/a couple of components here for emailing new and waitlisted users as part of the onboarding journey.

1. *`Waitlisted Email:`* When users create an account and are put on the waitlist, the ideal user experience is they get an email confirming they are on the list. <@U0AEL7C0BPB> I believe you are asking if we are already sending autoresponder messages to users when they are put on the waitlist, but <@U05BV05GYQH> you are confirming that is not currently happening at the moment. (I didn't think it was - but Mike let me know if you were told otherwise?)
2. `Welcome Email:`  For now, once we go to market I will manually send an email to users when they are OFF the waitlist. (This is why I need the list of users with their name, email, waitlist status, and date of joining). This removes the pressure of needing to get the email onboarding journey done before we start marketing. 
3. We want these emails to come from the info@sayso.news domain that you made recently <@U05BV05GYQH>. For the Welcome Emails, I just need access to the inbox in cerby. For the autoresponder Waitlist Emails - we'd need to discuss a. the priority of this and b. if there is a way to set this autoresponder up before we get to launch. I don't see a feasible way to do this manually, unfortunately.
<@U08HPM99N80> FYI since we didn't have a standup today, we deployed the update last night. The backoffice Users report today has the info you asked for
Also you should have access to the Cerby account - LMK if you don't see it

messages.text:
Random question, but is NextJS also domain driven development ?
Am i wrong or js late to the party ?
Wrong question :slightly_smiling_face:

Domain Driven Development is a design pattern. NextJS is a framework with a convention on how to place certain things so it can route/build things properly (and locate also for internal tooling).

DDD is about how you structure business logic and sys architecture. You can add a DDD layer in next js and that would look like

```/app
/domain
  /user
    User.ts
    UserRepository.ts
/infra
  /db ```
Interesting

Further reading: <https://timspark.com/blog/software-development-methods-overview/>

Also, unrelated but do checkout Gang of Four patterns

/**
 * Script to provision demo/test users with a known password for easy login.
 *
 * Instead of requiring email OTP, demo users can log in with PASSWORD as the
 * preferred challenge. The Cognito User Pool already supports both PASSWORD and
 * EMAIL_OTP as first auth factors, so no infrastructure changes are needed.
 *
 * Resolves AppSync endpoint and Cognito User Pool ID from SSM Parameter Store
 * (no Amplify dependency).
 *
 * Usage:
 *   npx tsx scripts/setup-demo-users.ts --env <environment> --emails <comma-separated> --password <password>
 *
 * Or via environment variables:
 *   DEMO_USER_EMAILS="demo@sayso.news,test@sayso.news" DEMO_USER_PASSWORD="DemoPass123!" \
 *     npx tsx scripts/setup-demo-users.ts --env stg
 *
 * Options:
 *   --env              Environment (dev, pr-123, stg, prod)
 *   --emails           Comma-separated list of demo user emails
 *   --password         Password to set for demo users
 *   --reset-password   Only reset password for existing users (skip user creation)
 *   --dry-run          Show what would be done without making changes
 *
 * Examples:
 *   npx tsx scripts/setup-demo-users.ts --env stg --emails "demo@sayso.news" --password "DemoPass123!"
 *   npx tsx scripts/setup-demo-users.ts --env dev --emails "demo@sayso.news" --password "DemoPass123!"
 *   npx tsx scripts/setup-demo-users.ts --env pr-123 --emails "<mailto:a@test.com|a@test.com>,b@test.com" --password "Test1234!"
 */
import { Sha256 } from '@aws-crypto/sha256-js'
import {
  AdminAddUserToGroupCommand,
  AdminCreateUserCommand,
  AdminGetUserCommand,
  AdminSetUserPasswordCommand,
  AdminUpdateUserAttributesCommand,
  CognitoIdentityProviderClient,
} from '@aws-sdk/client-cognito-identity-provider'
import { GetParameterCommand, SSMClient } from '@aws-sdk/client-ssm'
import { fromNodeProviderChain } from '@aws-sdk/credential-providers'
import { SignatureV4 } from '@smithy/signature-v4'

import { AuthGroups } from '../amplify/auth/AuthGroups'

// Constants
const AWS_REGION = process.env.AWS_REGION || 'us-east-1'
const PROJECT = process.env.PROJECT || 'sayso'

interface GraphQLResponse<T> {
  data?: T
  errors?: Array<{ message: string; path?: string[] }>
}

interface Args {
  env: string
  emails: string[]
  password: string
  dryRun: boolean
  resetPassword: boolean
}

/**
 * Resolve the environment ID used in SSM parameter paths.
 * For "pr-123" → "pr-123", for "stg" → "stg", etc.
 */
function resolveEnvId(env: string): string {
  return env
}

function parseArgs(): Args {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2)
  const result: Args = {
    env: '',
    emails: [],
    password: '',
    dryRun: false,
    resetPassword: false,
  }

  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
    const arg = args[i]
    switch (arg) {
      case '--env':
        result.env = args[++i] || ''
        break
      case '--emails':
        result.emails = (args[++i] || '')
          .split(',')
          .map(e => e.trim())
          .filter(Boolean)
        break
      case '--password':
        result.password = args[++i] || ''
        break
      case '--dry-run':
        result.dryRun = true
        break
      case '--reset-password':
        result.resetPassword = true
        break
      case '--help':
        console.log(`
Usage: npx tsx scripts/setup-demo-users.ts --env <environment> [options]

Options:
  --env              Environment (dev, pr-123, stg, prod) [required]
  --emails           Comma-separated demo user emails (or set DEMO_USER_EMAILS)
  --password         Password for demo users (or set DEMO_USER_PASSWORD)
  --reset-password   Only reset password for existing users (skip user creation)
  --dry-run          Show what would be done without making changes

Examples:
  npx tsx scripts/setup-demo-users.ts --env stg --emails "demo@sayso.news" --password "DemoPass123!"
  npx tsx scripts/setup-demo-users.ts --env dev --emails "demo@sayso.news" --password "DemoPass123!"
  npx tsx scripts/setup-demo-users.ts --env pr-123 --emails "<mailto:a@test.com|a@test.com>" --password "Test1234!"
`)
        process.exit(0)
    }
  }

  // Fall back to environment variables
  if (result.emails.length === 0 && process.env.DEMO_USER_EMAILS) {
    result.emails = process.env.DEMO_USER_EMAILS.split(',')
      .map(e => e.trim())
      .filter(Boolean)
  }
  if (!result.password && process.env.DEMO_USER_PASSWORD) {
    result.password = process.env.DEMO_USER_PASSWORD
  }

  if (!result.env) {
    console.error('Error: --env is required')
    process.exit(1)
  }
  if (result.emails.length === 0) {
    console.error('Error: --emails or DEMO_USER_EMAILS is required')
    process.exit(1)
  }
  if (!result.password) {
    console.error('Error: --password or DEMO_USER_PASSWORD is required')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  return result
}

// Reused from populate-pr-data.ts
function generateUniquePreferredUsername(email: string): string {
  const [localPart, domain] = email.split('@')

  let hash = 0
  for (let i = 0; i < localPart.length; i++) {
    const char = localPart.charCodeAt(i)
    hash = (hash << 5) - hash + char
    hash = hash & hash
  }
  for (let i = 0; i < domain.length; i++) {
    const char = domain.charCodeAt(i)
    hash = (hash << 3) - hash + char
    hash = hash & hash
  }

  const positiveHash = Math.abs(hash)
  const base36String = positiveHash.toString(36)

  let generatedId = base36String
  if (generatedId.length < 8) {
    const cleanLocalPart = localPart.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, '')
    const padding = cleanLocalPart.slice(0, 8 - generatedId.length)
    generatedId = generatedId + padding
  } else if (generatedId.length > 12) {
    generatedId = generatedId.slice(0, 12)
  }

  return `user_${generatedId}`
}

async function getSSMParam(
  ssmClient: SSMClient,
  paramName: string,
): Promise<string> {
  const result = await ssmClient.send(
    new GetParameterCommand({ Name: paramName }),
  )

  if (!result.Parameter?.Value) {
    throw new Error(`SSM parameter not found or empty: ${paramName}`)
  }

  return result.Parameter.Value
}

async function graphqlRequest<T>(
  endpoint: string,
  query: string,
  variables: Record<string, unknown> = {},
): Promise<GraphQLResponse<T>> {
  const url = new URL(endpoint)

  const request = {
    method: 'POST',
    protocol: url.protocol,
    hostname: url.hostname,
    path: url.pathname,
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      host: url.hostname,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }),
  }

  const signer = new SignatureV4({
    credentials: fromNodeProviderChain(),
    service: 'appsync',
    region: AWS_REGION,
    sha256: Sha256,
  })

  const signedRequest = await signer.sign(request)

  const response = await fetch(endpoint, {
    method: signedRequest.method,
    headers: signedRequest.headers,
    body: signedRequest.body,
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    const errorText = await response.text()
    throw new Error(
      `GraphQL request failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText}\n${errorText}`,
    )
  }

  return response.json() as Promise<GraphQLResponse<T>>
}

:thread: Media Processing Pipeline
Changes I think we should make
• Have 2 appsync resolvers, 1 which can return presigned URLs for client to upload files, another to kickstart the process after files have been uploaded which can return postID, so client can track the actual post, this will also remove save file out of the pipeline
• Decouple post and media from the pipeline, this will enable running tagging/moderation parallel to save processing time.
• Tag all media/process with `postId::mediaID`  so we can track things better.
• Add additional metadata like caption, postId to CF uploads
• Add monitoring so we can get slack update or email if something fails.
• I am still debating whether to keep the media processing as a state machine or make it queue based, i do like the UI that comes with state machines but right now the wiring feels like a lot.
I would also like to prioritize having a logic to ask the user to update the App if it is below a version, the media changes will definitely break app logic.

[2026-03-02T16:27-05:00] me: We can whiteboard this if needed.

messages.text:
:thread: Media Processing Pipeline
Changes I think we should make
• Have 2 appsync resolvers, 1 which can return presigned URLs for client to upload files, another to kickstart the process after files have been uploaded which can return postID, so client can track the actual post, this will also remove save file out of the pipeline
• Decouple post and media from the pipeline, this will enable running tagging/moderation parallel to save processing time.
• Tag all media/process with `postId::mediaID`  so we can track things better.
• Add additional metadata like caption, postId to CF uploads
• Add monitoring so we can get slack update or email if something fails.
• I am still debating whether to keep the media processing as a state machine or make it queue based, i do like the UI that comes with state machines but right now the wiring feels like a lot.

Agree on all points. The last one feels disconnected. Queue based and state machine are not mutually exclusive - unless I'm misreading your intent here.

Queues are about the order of processing items - in this case individual videos/images. The processing of item is done by the state machine which is basically executing a flowchart: `start > do something > if yes, do this; if no, do that... > end`
We can whiteboard this if needed.
Sounds good! I'll update my existing diagram and we can take it from there

<https://github.com/the-news-movement/tnm-aws-platform/blob/main/scripts/bastion-tunnel.sh|bastion-tunnel.sh> | ```
#!/bin/bash
# Opens an SSM port-forwarding tunnel to Aurora PostgreSQL via the bastion host.
# Prerequisites: AWS CLI v2, Session Manager plugin, AWS_PROFILE exported and logged in.
#
# Usage:
#   export AWS_PROFILE=stg-readonly   # or prod-readonly
#   aws sso login
#   ./scripts/bastion-tunnel.sh [local_port]

set -euo pipefail

LOCAL_PORT="${1:-5432}"
SSM_PORT=$((LOCAL_PORT + 1))

cleanup() {
  echo ""
  echo "Shutting down..."
  kill $(jobs -p) 2>/dev/null
  wait 2>/dev/null
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

if [[ -z "${AWS_PROFILE:-}" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: AWS_PROFILE is not set. Export it first, e.g.:"
  echo "  export AWS_PROFILE=stg-readonly"
  exit 1
fi

echo "Using AWS_PROFILE=$AWS_PROFILE"

echo "Fetching bastion instance ID..."
INSTANCE_ID=$(aws ssm get-parameter \
  --name "/sayso/bastion/instance-id" \
  --query 'Parameter.Value' \
  --output text)

echo "Fetching RDS Proxy endpoint..."
DB_HOST=$(aws ssm get-parameter \
  --name "/sayso/database/proxy-endpoint" \
  --query 'Parameter.Value' \
  --output text)

echo "Fetching database credentials..."
SECRET_ARN=$(aws ssm get-parameter \
  --name "/sayso/database/secret-arn" \
  --query 'Parameter.Value' \
  --output text)

DB_USER=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
  --secret-id "$SECRET_ARN" \
  --query SecretString \
  --output text | jq -r .username)

echo ""
echo "========================================="
echo " Tunnel ready to start"
echo "========================================="
echo " Host (in pgAdmin): 127.0.0.1"
echo " Port:              $LOCAL_PORT"
echo " Database:          sayso"
echo " Username:          $DB_USER"
echo " SSL Mode:          require"
echo ""
echo " Password: run this in another terminal:"
echo "   aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \\"
echo "     --secret-id \"$SECRET_ARN\" \\"
echo "     --query SecretString --output text | jq -r .password"
echo "========================================="
echo ""
echo "Starting SSM tunnel on 0.0.0.0:$LOCAL_PORT (Ctrl+C to stop)..."

# SSM tunnel binds to 127.0.0.1 only, so we use socat to relay from 0.0.0.0
# This allows Windows pgAdmin to reach the tunnel running inside WSL.
aws ssm start-session \
  --target "$INSTANCE_ID" \
  --document-name AWS-StartPortForwardingSessionToRemoteHost \
  --parameters "{\"host\":[\"$DB_HOST\"],\"portNumber\":[\"5432\"],\"localPortNumber\":[\"$SSM_PORT\"]}" &

# Wait for SSM tunnel to be ready
sleep 3

echo "Starting socat relay 0.0.0.0:$LOCAL_PORT -> 127.0.0.1:$SSM_PORT..."
socat TCP-LISTEN:$LOCAL_PORT,fork,reuseaddr,bind=0.0.0.0 TCP:127.0.0.1:$SSM_PORT

```

#151 refactor: separate stacks & infra isolation | *Overview*

This PR refactors the monolithic CDK infrastructure into independent, isolated stacks with strict boundary enforcement. The goal is to enable independent deployments, reduce blast radius, and prevent accidental cross-stack coupling.

*Key Changes*

*:building_construction: Architecture Refactoring*

*Stack Separation*
• Split monolithic stack into 8 independent stacks:  
   • `platform-networking` - VPC, subnets, NAT gateways  
   • `platform-vpc-endpoints` - VPC Interface and Gateway endpoints  
   • `platform-sayso-auth` - Cognito (no networking dependencies)  
   • `platform-sayso-search` - OpenSearch Serverless  
   • `platform-sayso-database` - Aurora PostgreSQL  
   • `platform-sayso-ml` - SageMaker endpoints and training  
   • `platform-sayso-pipeline` - Kinesis/Glue/Athena  
   • `platform-kudosbot` - KudosBot infrastructure
*Cross-Stack Communication*
• Stacks communicate via CloudFormation exports (`Fn.importValue()`)
• CDC integration uses deterministic role naming to avoid circular dependencies
• No runtime cross-stack references needed (stacks are fully independent)

*:lock: Network Isolation*

*Dedicated Subnets*
• Created dedicated VPC Endpoint subnets (`/27` CIDR blocks) owned by NetworkingStack
• Project-specific subnet allocations (Sayso: `/24`, KudosBot: `/28`)
• Aurora and SageMaker get dedicated isolated subnets
*S3 Gateway Endpoint Fix*
• Changed from `SubnetType` enum to explicit subnet selections
• Prevents arbitrary subnet selection at deployment time
• Added `privateSubnetsForS3` and `isolatedSubnetsForS3` props to NetworkingStackProps
*Configurable Availability Zones*
• Moved hardcoded AZs to environment configuration
• Supports 2-3 AZ deployments based on region

*:shield: Security Improvements*

*CDC Consumer IAM*
• Removed invalid `aoss:collection` IAM condition (not a valid OpenSearch Serverless condition key)
• Scoped IAM resources to account/region: `arn:aws:aoss:${Aws.REGION}:${Aws.ACCOUNT_ID}:collection/*`
• Added CDC consumer role to OpenSearch data access policy
*OpenSearch Access Policy*
• Added `additionalWriterRoleArns` prop for cross-stack role authorization
• Pre-authorizes CDC consumer role using deterministic naming pattern
• Both IAM role ARN and assumed-role ARN formats included for Lambda execution

*:books: Documentation*

*Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)*
• ADR-001: Shared VPC Architecture
• ADR-002: Independent Stack Architecture
• ADR-003: Project-Specific Subnet Isolation
• ADR-004: Strict Stack Boundary Enforcement
• ADR-005: Monorepo with Strict Boundaries

*:wrench: Tooling*

*Stack Boundary Checker*
• Custom ESLint rule (`eslint-rules/stack-boundaries.mjs`)
• CLI script (`scripts/check-stack-boundaries.ts`)
• Prevents imports across stack boundaries
• Validates cross-stack reference patterns

*:package: CI/CD Updates*

• Updated GitHub workflows for multi-stack deployment
• Added CODEOWNERS file
• Improved PR checks and linting

*Breaking Changes*

• Stack names changed from single stack to `platform-*` prefix convention
• VpcEndpointsStack now requires explicit subnet selections instead of SubnetType
• CDC consumer no longer imports `openSearchWriterRoleArn` (uses deterministic naming) | https://github.com/the-news-movement/tnm-aws-platform/pull/151

#281 feat: resolve full media URLs server-side & add custom CDN domain :sparkles: | *Summary*

This change moves media URL resolution to the backend so the iOS app no longer has to assemble URLs client-side.

*Media URL resolution*

• `mapPostToGraphQL` now converts `rawAssetUrl` into a full CloudFront URL and returns it as `streamUrl`.
• Image posts now return a usable URL like  
`<https://cdn.svc.sayso.news/posts/>...` instead of `null`.
• Video posts remain unchanged and continue returning Cloudflare HLS URLs.
• `rawAssetUrl` is still returned for backward compatibility.
• All 7 resolvers that use `mapPostToGraphQL` were updated to pass `cloudfrontBaseUrl`.

*Custom CDN domain*

CloudFront now uses a proper domain instead of the default `*.<http://cloudfront.net|cloudfront.net>`.
Domains by environment:
• *prod* → `cdn.svc.sayso.news`
• *stg* → `cdn.stg.svc.sayso.news`
• *dev* → `cdn-dev.stg.svc.sayso.news`
PR environments are intentionally skipped to avoid the overhead of creating and cleaning up ACM certificates.
The setup includes:
• ACM certificate with DNS validation
• Route53 alias record pointing to the distribution
All of this is provisioned automatically.

*Infrastructure impact*

No additional infra changes were required.
• `MEDIA_CLOUDFRONT_URL` is already configured on all AppSync lambdas.
• The new domain flows through automatically via the existing SSM parameter and AppConfig setup.

*iOS impact*

Once this is deployed, the iOS app can stop resolving image URLs manually.
`resolvePictureURL` can be removed and the app can simply use `streamUrl` for both images and videos.

*Test plan*

• Deploy to *dev* and confirm `streamUrl` returns full URLs like  
`<https://cdn-dev.stg.svc.sayso.news/>...` for image posts
• Verify video posts still return Cloudflare HLS URLs in `streamUrl`
• Confirm the ACM certificate validates successfully
• Verify the custom CDN domain resolves correctly
• Check AppConfig and confirm `cloudfrontUrl` reflects the new domain | https://github.com/the-news-movement/who-knows-aws-services/pull/281

Why we need those stupid double quotes

> PostgreSQL folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase. Your tables were created with double-quoted mixed-case names (e.g. `"Posts"`, `"Media"`), so Postgres stored them as `Posts` not `posts`. Without quotes, `Posts` becomes `posts`, which doesn't exist.

<https://github.com/the-news-movement/who-knows-aws-services/blob/main/scripts/athena_to_sheets.py|athena_to_sheets.py> | ```
"""
Athena → Google Sheets: Daily Active Users

Queries AWS Athena for daily active users and writes results to a Google Sheet.

Setup:
  1. pip install "pyathena[pandas]" gspread google-auth
  2. Create a Google Cloud project → enable Google Sheets API
  3. Create a Service Account → download the JSON key file
  4. Share the target Google Sheet with the service account email (Editor access)
  5. Set the environment variables below (or use a .env file)

Usage:
  python scripts/athena_to_sheets.py

Schedule daily:
  crontab -e → 0 9 * * * /path/to/venv/bin/python /path/to/athena_to_sheets.py
"""

import os
import logging
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
from pyathena import connect
from pyathena.pandas.cursor import PandasCursor
import gspread

logging.basicConfig(level=<http://logging.INFO|logging.INFO>, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# --- Config (set these as env vars) ---
# Database: sayso_signals_raw | Table: signals
# Workgroup: sayso-signals-{env}-ue1-athena-wg-tnm
# SSM param for results bucket: /sayso/signals/analytics/athena-results-bucket-name
ATHENA_DATABASE = os.environ.get("ATHENA_DATABASE", "sayso_signals_raw")
ATHENA_S3_OUTPUT = os.environ.get("ATHENA_S3_OUTPUT", "<s3://sayso-athresults-prod-ue1-s3-tnm/data-analyst/>")
ATHENA_WORKGROUP = os.environ.get("ATHENA_WORKGROUP", "sayso-dasignals-prod-ue1-ath-tnm-wg")
AWS_REGION = os.environ.get("AWS_REGION", "us-east-1")
GOOGLE_SHEET_ID = os.environ.get("GOOGLE_SHEET_ID", "1u9H83r9QZ8PhOkX0dOOMWgsQZsqycdd35znOOqaxKhE")
GOOGLE_SA_KEY_PATH = os.environ.get("GOOGLE_SA_KEY_PATH", "sayso-athena-service-account.json")

# --- Athena query: Daily Active Users (last 30 days) ---
# Queries sayso_analytics.user_metrics for daily platform metrics.
# activeusersdaily = distinct users who posted, liked, or commented that day.
# ETL runs daily at 04:30 UTC.
QUERY = """
SELECT
    snapshotdate AS date,
    activeusersdaily AS active_users,
    newusersdaily AS new_users,
    newpostsdaily AS new_posts,
    totalusers AS total_users,
    deletedusersdaily AS deleted_users
FROM sayso_analytics.user_metrics
WHERE snapshotdate >= CAST(CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30' DAY AS VARCHAR)
ORDER BY snapshotdate DESC
"""


def query_athena(query: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Run a query against Athena and return a DataFrame."""
    <http://log.info|log.info>("Connecting to Athena (database=%s, region=%s)", ATHENA_DATABASE, AWS_REGION)
    conn = connect(
        s3_staging_dir=ATHENA_S3_OUTPUT,
        region_name=AWS_REGION,
        schema_name=ATHENA_DATABASE,
        work_group=ATHENA_WORKGROUP,
        cursor_class=PandasCursor,
    )
    <http://log.info|log.info>("Executing query...")
    df = pd.read_sql(query, conn)
    <http://log.info|log.info>("Query returned %d rows", len(df))
    return df


def write_to_sheet(df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    """Write a DataFrame to a Google Sheet, replacing existing content."""
    script_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    sa_key_path = script_dir / GOOGLE_SA_KEY_PATH

    gc = gspread.service_account(filename=str(sa_key_path))

    sheet = gc.open_by_key(GOOGLE_SHEET_ID).sheet1
    <http://log.info|log.info>("Writing to Google Sheet: %s", GOOGLE_SHEET_ID)

    # Clear and write fresh data
    sheet.clear()

    # Header row
    headers = df.columns.tolist()
    # Convert all values to strings to avoid serialization issues (dates, etc.)
    rows = df.astype(str).values.tolist()

    sheet.update(values=[headers] + rows, range_name="A1")

    # Add a metadata note in the corner
    last_col = chr(ord("A") + len(headers))  # next column after data
    sheet.update_acell(f"{last_col}1", f"Last updated: {datetime.now().isoformat(timespec='minutes')}")

    <http://log.info|log.info>("Sheet updated with %d rows", len(rows))


def main():
    df = query_athena(QUERY)
    if df.empty:
        log.warning("No results returned from Athena query")
        return
    write_to_sheet(df)
    <http://log.info|log.info>("Done!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

[2026-03-23T12:15-04:00] me: The restore script inserts rows for tables with `preserveId: false` (like Media) by omitting the `id` column, letting PostgreSQL's auto-increment sequence assign IDs. After restoring hundreds of rows, the sequence advances. But the sequence only tracks what _it_ generated — if the restore is run multiple times or the sequence was already at a value lower than MAX(id), new inserts collide with existing rows. The real issue: the `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` silently skips duplicate rows during restore, but the sequence *doesn't advance* for skipped rows. After restore, `nextval()` can return an ID that already exists in the table, causing collisions on subsequent application inserts. I had the resets but removed them in my last commit thinking we won't need them as we're inserting. I didn't think about the skipped rows :man-facepalming:

But the sequence only tracks what _it_ generated — if the restore is run multiple times or the sequence was already at a value lower than MAX(id), new inserts collide with existing rows.

The real issue: the `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` silently skips duplicate rows during restore, but the sequence *doesn't advance* for skipped rows. After restore, `nextval()` can return an ID that already exists in the table, causing collisions on subsequent application inserts.

Let’s release on Monday and make sure we are aligned with Mike and Lizzie for paid marketing, as well as Hannah for the embargo date and trying to time this with some new UI. My immediate thoughts are:

1. Go ahead and release on Monday, and ensure all paid marketing / the creator links / SaySo.news pages direct to the new app. So all net new subscribers will start going to the public app asap. 
2. Wait to migrate existing users until we release the UI changes (next week? :crossed_fingers::skin-tone-4:), so we can create messaging that makes this feel exciting (new look and feel!) and like a real reason for users to need to get a new app, instead of a friction point. This gives us a little time to get the language on Monday and add the migration banner to the old app. 
However, I realize that might mean the dev team is across two apps at once. So tell me to kick rocks if that's not doable.

The last part is the kicker.

• updating sayso download link: easy
• updating creators links: not required 
• maintaining 2 apps: kicker
We also should test the new app. I can assign it on testflight so this group can do a few rounds just to make sure wires are all connected properly

Review against these standards:

## Code Quality
- Minimal and pragmatic — no over-engineering, no premature abstractions
- No unnecessary config, or "just in case" code

- Follow language style guides

- No hardcoded secrets, credentials, or API keys
- No injection vulnerabilities (SQL, XSS, command injection)
- Parameterized queries for database access

/* Commented since we don't have proper testing and I don't want to create noise 

## Testing
- All code changes must include unit tests
- Integration tests for external boundaries (APIs, databases, file I/O)

*/

## Output Format
Format your response as a GitHub PR comment in markdown with EXACTLY these section headers:

### Must Fix
Critical issues that must be resolved before merging. Number each item. If none, write "None."

### Should Consider
Important improvements that should be addressed. Number each item. If none, write "None."

### Minor
Non-blocking nits and style suggestions. These will NOT be auto-fixed.

### Looks Good
What the PR does well.

#217 chore: agentic setup | I gave it the following task:

```
We want to add support for search synonyms and aliases for SaySo. Start with a plan only and do not edit files yet.

Think holistically:
- whether this belongs in tnm-aws-platform or an application repo
- long-term platform implications
- cost implications
- how this affects future search design
- whether this creates a reusable pattern or a one-off
- what alternatives exist

```

and it produced the following plan:
Search Synonyms & Aliases for SaySo 

*Context*

SaySo's search today is Postgres `ILIKE` substring matching on three resolvers  
(<src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/|v2/client/search/>):
• `searchPosts` → `posts.caption ILIKE %q%`
• `searchTopics` → `topics.name ILIKE %q%`
• `searchUsers` → `users.username ILIKE %q% OR users.name ILIKE %q%`
A user typing "AI" finds nothing about "artificial intelligence"; "POTUS" misses  
"president"; "DJT" misses "Donald Trump". The goal is *user-facing search recall*:  
expand the query into known synonym/alias terms before hitting the database.

*Strategic context (informs scope, not the implementation)*

• The platform repo (`tnm-aws-platform`) has provisioned an OpenSearch Serverless  
`content-search` collection (<../../../tnm-aws-platform/src/domains/sayso/search/OpenSearchConstruct.ts#L207|OpenSearchConstruct.ts:207>)  
with a `synonym_filter` baked into the analyzer  
(<../../../tnm-aws-platform/src/lambda/opensearch/opensearch-index-manager/index.js#L273-L276|opensearch-index-manager/index.js:273-276>),  
but it is *dormant — no data flowing*, and SaySo's resolvers do not consume it.  
We treat OpenSearch as future work and do *not* build against it here.
• The synonym format we choose is intentionally compatible with OpenSearch's native  
`synonym` filter (comma-separated terms per group), so if/when the OpenSearch  
migration revives, the same vocabulary file can be lifted into analyzer config.
• Decision: *SaySo-only, engineer-managed via PR, lives in this repo*. No platform  
changes, no new infrastructure, no new database tables, no admin UI.

*Approach*

Build a static synonym/alias dictionary as a TypeScript module in  
`src/appsync-resolvers/shared/`, and call a pure `expandQuery()` helper from each of  
the three search resolvers to convert the raw user query into a set of OR'd `ILIKE`  
clauses against the existing columns.

*Vocabulary format*

Two complementary structures, both compile-time constants:
• *Synonym groups* — bidirectional. Any term in a group matches the others.  
Format mirrors OpenSearch's `synonym` filter so a future port is mechanical.  
export const SYNONYM_GROUPS: ReadonlyArray<ReadonlyArray<string>> = [  
  ['ai', 'artificial intelligence', 'machine learning', 'ml'],  
  ['eu', 'european union'],  
  ['potus', 'president of the united states'],  
  // ...  
]
• *Aliases* — directional, `alias → canonical`. Use when there's a clear canonical  
form (typically a Topic name or proper noun) we want to bias toward.  
export const ALIASES: Record<string, string> = {  
  djt: 'donald trump',  
  aoc: 'alexandria ocasio-cortez',  
  // ...  
}
Internally both collapse into the same expansion table for lookup; the split exists  
purely so engineers writing entries can express intent (group vs. canonicalize).

*Query expansion*

A single pure function in <src/appsync-resolvers/shared/search-synonyms.ts|search-synonyms.ts>:

export function expandQuery(rawQuery: string): string[]

Behavior:
1. Trim + lowercase the query.
2. Look up the whole query string in the expansion table.
3. Return `[normalizedQuery, ...expansions]`, de-duplicated, original first.
4. If no match, return `[normalizedQuery]` (1-element array — callers always  
iterate, so the path with no synonyms is identical to today's behavior).
*Phase 1 deliberately does NOT tokenize multi-word queries.* Whole-phrase match  
only. Tokenized per-word expansion ("donald trump biden" → expand each token)  
adds noise and is a fast-follow if we see search-quality data demanding it. We  
revisit after instrumenting `search_no_results` events from the iOS client  
(already tracked, per <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/|Phase 1 exploration>).

*Resolver wiring*

Each of the three handlers does the same shape of change: derive an array of  
search terms once, then change the Sequelize `where` clause from a single  
`ILIKE` to `Op.or` over the expanded terms.
*Posts* — <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/posts/handler.ts|v2/client/search/posts/handler.ts> and <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/posts/queries.ts|v2/client/search/posts/queries.ts>:

const terms = expandQuery(rawQuery).map(t => `%${t}%`)
// queries.ts:
where: {
  [Op.or]: terms.map(t => ({ caption: { [Op.iLike]: t } })),
  status: 'PUBLISHED',
  moderationStatus: MediaModerationStatus.APPROVED,
  banned: false,
  ...(blockedUserIds.length > 0 && { userId: { [Op.notIn]: blockedUserIds } }),
}

*Topics* — <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/topics/handler.ts|v2/client/search/topics/handler.ts>:  
single column (`name`); same `Op.or` shape.
*Users* — <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/users/handler.ts|v2/client/search/users/handler.ts>:  
two columns (`username`, `name`) and existing `Op.or`. Inner OR becomes the  
cross-product `terms × columns`:

[Op.or]: terms.flatMap(t => [
  { username: { [Op.iLike]: t } },
  { name: { [Op.iLike]: t } },
])

`findAndCountAll` (posts) and `findAll` (topics/users) semantics are preserved;  
`count` and `contributorsCount` still reflect the full expanded query set, which  
is the desired behavior.

*What stays the same*

• GraphQL schema — no changes.
• Pagination (`limit + 1` cursor pattern), `nextToken` encoding, ordering by  
`publishedAt DESC`.
• Authorization, block filtering, moderation gates.
• AppSync wiring in <lib/constructs/AppSyncDataSources.ts|AppSyncDataSources.ts>.

*Cost & performance*

• *No infrastructure cost.* Pure code change.
• *Query cost:* each expansion adds an OR-clause `ILIKE` on the same column.  
At current scale (no production traffic data, but tables are small) Postgres  
will seq-scan + filter regardless of clause count — ILIKE substring queries  
do not use the existing btree indexes. Worst case ~5-10x expansion factor on  
typical synonym entries; query plan stays linear in clause count.
• *Forward path:* when query volume justifies it, add a `pg_trgm` GIN index  
on `posts.caption`, `topics.name`, `users.name`, `users.username`. Each `ILIKE`  
clause can then use the index; expansion remains forward-compatible. This is  
the cheapest performance win and orthogonal to the synonym work — track it  
separately.

*Files to change*

| File                                                       | Change                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <src/appsync-resolvers/shared/search-synonyms.ts>          | *New.* SYNONYM_GROUPS, ALIASES, expandQuery(). Seed with ~15-30 high-value entries. |
| <src/appsync-resolvers/shared/search-synonyms.test.ts>     | *New.* Unit tests for expandQuery.                                                  |
| <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/posts/queries.ts>  | Accept terms: string[] instead of searchTerm: string; build Op.or clause.           |
| <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/posts/handler.ts>  | Call expandQuery(rawQuery) and pass terms to query.                                 |
| <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/topics/handler.ts> | Same pattern (inline query).                                                        |
| <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/users/handler.ts>  | Same pattern; cross-product over username + name.                                   |

No schema changes, no migrations, no CDK changes, no platform-repo changes.

*Reuse check*

transcript:
[2026-05-15T09:39-04:00] U0AU9EKU81K: Hey <@U05BV05GYQH>, working on <https://app.asana.com/1/1206660498759239/project/1211854325083548/task/1214542735108150?focus=true|DEV-1138> (refresh-token expiry on launch). Before fix: user saw a blocking "Analytics unavailable / AuthError 7" modal and got stuck on Main with no way forward. After: no modal, the app force-logs them out to landing with a clear "Session expired" alert so they can sign in again. The fix itself solves the UX, but we still have no prod signal for this bug. So I'm thinking it'd be right to add a `session_expired` lifecycle event (same pattern as `user_signout`, stamped with the outgoing user_id) — so we can measure how often users actually hit this post-fix and triage if reports keep coming in. Two questions: 1. OK to add it? 2. If yes — Marin suggested Kinesis-only (not AppsFlyer) since it's diagnostic, not attribution. Sound right? Happy to drop if it doesn't fit your direction.
[2026-05-15T15:05-04:00] U0AU9EKU81K: :pray: would love your input when you get a chance
[2026-05-15T16:00-04:00] me: 1 - excellent idea 2- correct
[2026-05-15T17:08-04:00] U0AU9EKU81K: Thanks!
